Clinical AI now has journals of its own. *NEJM AI*, *The Lancet Digital Health* and *npj Digital Medicine* publish every week, JAMA curates its AI work in JAMA+ AI, and *Nature Medicine* carries a steady stream of model evaluations. Most of it is retrospective and single-site. The papers that should change what we do — prospective trials, honest external validations, rigorous tests of large language models against clinicians — are easy to miss among the rest.

Every two weeks, [Claude](https://claude.ai) searches PubMed across those dedicated AI journals, the major general journals, and the transplantation and nephrology journals I read anyway. It shortlists up to eight papers and summarises each one in plain language: what the tool was, what it was measured against, and whether the result holds outside the development data. Every citation is checked against PubMed before I review the issue and publish it.

It is a deliberately small, curated first pass, not a complete index, and no substitute for reading the primary sources. Always verify against the original publication before relying on anything here.

The pipeline is the same one that runs [Kidney Watch](/briefings.qmd), my weekly kidney transplantation digest. I described how it works in [From a literature-search skill to a self-running evidence digest](/posts/automated-literature-watch/).

**Found this useful?** Get each new issue by email (see below), or follow via the [RSS feed](/ai-watch.xml). Leave a comment below, here for general feedback or under any individual issue.
